WHAT CHANGED IN THE FIX ROUND, against the four confirmed findings. Nothing else was touched.

Finding 1 (AG0023/AG0029 wrong-assembly hole) — fixed in three files.
- analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers/OneDoorRule.cs: RegisterBoundariesAndEngineGates took ONE isInScope predicate and fed it to the pinned-unchanged Boundaries gate, the new Engine call gate and both new Engine type-reference lenses. It now takes isInScopeFromBoundaries and isInScopeFromEngine separately. This is the split the fix direction authorized and Tim's condition asked for (\"Keep any required scope expansion on the Engine-facing checks\") — the Boundaries gate provably keeps its exact pre-existing filter rather than relying on an argument no current fixture happens to exercise the difference of.
- analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers/OneDoorIntoCrossPlatformAnalyzer.cs: adds IsCrossPlatformCoreTypeFromEngine = core assembly OR (namespace AgentGuard.CrossPlatform AND NOT one of the three genuine per-OS assemblies, via the already-existing CrossPlatformBoundary.IsPerOsImplementationAssembly). The old assembly-only predicate stays and is what the Boundaries gate still receives.
- analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers/OneDoorIntoPerOsAnalyzer.cs: keeps the per-OS assembly filter on both gates, and records in code why that is THIS rule's correct predicate rather than a copy of the sibling's.

THE PARTITION, STATED EXPLICITLY (the fix direction required one rule to own the shared-namespace foreign squatter, and named this as the hard part).
AG0023 owns every assembly that squats the shared AgentGuard.CrossPlatform namespace and is not one of the three genuine per-OS implementations. AG0029 owns exactly those three. Exactly one rule reports such a decoy; the other is silent; neither reports the other's legitimate traffic.
The direction is forced by the two door identities, not chosen by preference:
- AG0023's door is matched with its declaring assembly pinned (WellKnownType.IsInAssembly(type, RootName, \"CrossPlatformAdapters\", RootName)), so a squatter drawn into its scope lands in scope and then FAILS the door test — the exact shape AG0040 already proves.
- AG0029's door is matched on namespace plus name ALONE, deliberately (PlatformServices is declared in all three per-OS assemblies under that same namespace; see PlatformFactory.IsFactoryType's own comment). Its assembly filter IS its door's assembly identity. Widening it would make a decoy PlatformServices PASS the door test and be ACCEPTED at the permitted site — the widening that closes the hole for the sibling would open one here.
So the fix direction's literal \"for AG0029, admit the symmetric case\" was NOT applied: symmetric admission would have both rules claim the same foreign assembly (the overlap the same document forbids) and would turn AG0029 from silent into permissive.
